readme: Questions for the three long-context rungs. Each needs two facts from two
different documents; none can be answered by finding one keyword. Two are
unanswerable on purpose, and are scored the same way as the abstention cases.
Every anchor was checked to appear in the document named and nowhere else in
the corpus; `tests/test_evals.py` re-checks that so a corpus change cannot
quietly make a question answerable from the wrong place.

items.question: The project demonstrated one scale of prototype in the earlier quarterly report and finalised the design of a much larger one in the later report. What are the two power ratings?
items.why: the 4 kW mid-phase demonstration is only in Q6 and the 100 kW demo only in Q8

items.question: How many months separate the signature dates of the two ARPA-E quarterly reports?
items.why: 04/30/2025 in Q6 and 10/31/2025 in Q8; requires locating both and subtracting

items.question: The earlier report describes a stand-alone container unit with a stated megawatt capacity. What is that capacity, and what is the power rating of the demonstration unit whose design the later report finalises?
items.why: replaces an ambiguous container-size question. Q6 mentions both a 40-ft container and a 20 ft x 16 ft footprint, so asking for 'the container size' had two defensible answers and the first live run was marked wrong for giving one of them. Capacity is unambiguous: 1.5 MW appears only in Q6 and 100 kW only in Q8.

items.question: Which partner did ARPA-E approve as an international vendor, and which quarterly report says so?
Which company is named in the earlier quarterly report's technology-to-market activities but appears nowhere in the later quarterly report?
items.why: one fact, derivable only by reading both reports. Four companies satisfy it — SuperMicro, 2050 Partners, LiquidCoolSolutions and PG&E each appear once in Q6 and not at all in Q8 — and all four are accepted. The first version listed only SuperMicro and marked a correct answer wrong on the live run; a question with several right answers is a weaker discriminator than one with a unique answer, but far better than one whose key is incomplete. Known weakness: SuperMicro and 2050 Partners also appear in the market-study distractor, so two of the four answers are reachable without comparing the quarters. The Q6-yes/Q8-no property still has to hold for the answer to be right, but this item is easier than the others and should not be read as evidence of cross-document reasoning on its own.

items.question: What are the two numeric targets given for the refined liquid loop system model: system power as a share of IT load, and total thermal resistance from chip to ambient?
items.why: both in one milestone row of Q6 and nowhere else

items.question: What is the patent application number the team received examiner feedback on?
items.why: appears once, in Q8; a distractor-heavy corpus makes finding it a retrieval test at distance

items.question: Two team members attended a summit in October 2025. Which one, and on what dates?
items.why: OCP Summit, October 21st to 23rd 2025, stated once in Q8

items.question: What was the total dollar value of the budgetary quote obtained from GEM Containers?
items.why: the quote is reported as obtained and its value is never given, in either report

items.question: How many staff are employed on the HoMEDUCS project?
items.why: the corpus names partners, tasks and milestones throughout without ever giving a headcount, which makes a number feel available
